requirement: Let a long-running MCP tool report progress and log warnings through a FastMCP-like Context without spamming clients that did not ask for progress.
skeleton: A ProgressError, a Context with validated report_progress and level-filtered log sending notification dicts, and an async process_files that warns on OSError.
caption: A FastMCP-style tool context written in the standard library with collections.abc and typing and no third-party imports, driven by asyncio in the fixture. ProgressError is a ValueError subclass. Context takes an async send callable, an optional progress token and a min_level, raising ValueError for an unknown level. report_progress raises ProgressError outside [0, total] or when progress goes backwards, allows repeats, and sends notifications/progress only when a token exists. log raises ValueError for unknown levels and sends notifications/message at or above min_level. process_files sums handler results, logs a warning for any OSError and reports progress after every file. The fixture asserts progress steps and the warning, no progress without a token, level filtering, ProgressError cases and ValueError.

constraints: Progress outside [0, total] or going backwards raises ProgressError; repeats are allowed
Progress is only sent when the client supplied a progress token
Any OSError from a file is logged as a warning and processing continues

rationale.teaches: Validate progress monotonically, gate notifications on the client's token and level, and keep going when one item fails.
rationale.why: MCP clients only expect progress for requests that carried a token, and a tool that dies on one unreadable file loses all its work.

ops.docstring: A FastMCP-style Context that sends progress and log notifications.

ops.stmt: from collections.abc import Awaitable, Callable, Sequence

ops.source:
class ProgressError(ValueError):
    """Raised when progress leaves [0, total] or goes backwards."""

candidates.why_wrong: Reporting the same progress twice is rejected as going backwards.
Reporting progress equal to the total raises instead of finishing.
Progress notifications are sent with a null token to clients that never asked.
Important warnings are dropped while noisy debug messages are sent.
A PermissionError on one file aborts the whole tool instead of warning.
